title: Household cooking in Nepal: An economic analysis
Landscape efficiency frontiers for biodiversity, climate mitigation, and net economic value
abstract: Balancing biodiversity, climate and economic development means making difficult choices about how land is used. Stephen Polasky, Regents Professor and Fesler-Lampert Professor of Ecological/Environmental Economics at the University of Minnesota, explores the trade-offs between competing demands for land. Meeting biodiversity, climate, and economic development goals requires careful consideration of how to utilize land and the potential tradeoffs among different goals. Land used in one way, such as to grow crops to help meet food demand, cannot also be devoted to another use, such as maintaining natural habitat for biodiversity and increased carbon sequestration.
abstract_zh: 平衡生物多样性、气候与经济发展，意味着需要在土地利用方面做出艰难的选择。明尼苏达大学生态/环境经济学讲席教授（Regents Professor）、费斯勒-兰珀特讲座教授（Fesler-Lampert Professor）Stephen Polasky探讨了土地竞争性需求之间的权衡。实现生物多样性、气候和经济发展目标，需要审慎考虑如何利用土地，以及不同目标之间潜在的取舍。一块土地若用于种植作物以满足粮食需求，就不能同时用于维持生物多样性的自然栖息地或增加碳封存。

title: Economic and policy analysis of cleaner technologies for brick production in Nepal
Identifying child growth effects of elevated pollution levels during pregnancy
abstract: Poor air quality is known to be one of the leading contributors to poor child health globally, and a wealth of evidence has linked pollution exposure during pregnancy to adverse birth and early-life outcomes. While there is some evidence pollution exposure during pregnancy is associated with slowed child growth, this evidence is largely limited to empirical settings in which it is difficult to disentangle the role of pollution from other co-varying factors. Here we rely on quasi-random variation in pollution conditions induced by thermal inversions to estimate the impact of pollution spikes during pregnancy on childhood stunting. We find that thermal inversions during pregnancy worsen air quality and increase the likelihood of childhood stunting, but only in places with poor baseline air quality and particularly for younger children and in lower-wealth communities. Our estimates imply that a 1  µg m−3 increase in average PM2.5 concentration during pregnancy increases the probability of stunting by an average of 4.1 percentage points (95% CI: 0.2–8.0). This translates to an 11.2% increase (95% CI: 0.6%–21.9%) in stunting risk from the sample baseline of 37% children stunted. Our results suggest that policies that limit baseline daily PM2.5 levels, particularly during seasons when thermal inversions are more frequent, have potential to generate meaningful improvements in long-run child outcomes.
abstract_zh: 空气质量差是全球儿童健康状况不佳的主要原因之一，大量证据表明，孕期接触污染与出生和婴幼儿期的不良结局有关。虽然有一些证据表明孕期污染暴露与儿童生长放缓相关，但这些证据大多局限于难以将污染的作用与其他共变因素区分开来的经验情境中。在此，我们利用热力学逆温（thermal inversions）引起的污染状况的准随机变化，估计孕期污染峰值对儿童发育迟缓（stunting）的影响。我们发现，孕期的热力学逆温会恶化空气质量，并增加儿童发育迟缓的可能性，但这仅发生在基线空气质量较差的地区，且对年幼儿童和低收入社区的儿童尤为明显。我们的估计表明，孕期平均PM2.5浓度每增加1 µg m−3，发育迟缓的概率平均增加4.1个百分点（95%置信区间：0.2–8.0）。这相当于在样本基线发育迟缓率为37%的基础上，发育迟缓风险增加11.2%（95%置信区间：0.6%–21.9%）。我们的结果表明，限制日常基线PM2.5水平的政策，特别是在热力学逆温更频繁的季节，有可能对儿童的长期发展产生有意义的改善。

Does the Environment Matter for Poverty Reduction? The Role of Soil Fertility and Vegetation Vigor in Poverty Reduction
abstract: The debate on the environment-poverty nexus is inconclusive, with past research unable to identify the causal dynamics. This paper uses a unique global panel data set that links (survey and census derived) poverty data to measures of environmental quality at the subnational level. The analysis uses vegetation vigor as a proxy for above-ground environmental quality and soil fertility as proxy for below-ground environmental quality. Rainfall is used to account for endogeneity issues in an instrumental variable approach. This is the first global study using quasi-experimental methods to uncover to what degree environmental quality matters for poverty reduction. The paper draws three main conclusions. (1) The environment matters for poverty reduction. The panel regression suggests that a 10 percent increase in vegetation vigor is associated with a poverty headcount ratio reduction of nearly 0.7 percentage point in rural areas, and 1 percentage point in Sub-Saharan Africa. A 10 percent increase in soil quality leads to a roughly 2 percentage point decrease in poverty rates in rural areas and in Sub-Saharan Africa. (2) The effects of environmental quality on poverty are stronger than its effects on average income, suggesting that the poor benefit disproportionately from environmental quality. (3) In situ environmental quality improvements are pro-poor, in contrast to urbanization. Although urbanization has highly significant and sizable correlations with GDP per capita, it is not significantly correlated with poverty reduction.
abstract_zh: 关于环境与贫困之间关系的争论尚无定论，以往研究无法识别其中的因果动态。本文利用一个独特的全球面板数据集，将（基于调查和普查得出的）贫困数据与次国家层面的环境质量指标相联系。分析以植被活力作为地表以上环境质量的代理变量，以土壤肥力作为地表以下环境质量的代理变量。我们使用降雨量作为工具变量来解决内生性问题。这是首个运用准实验方法揭示环境质量在多大程度上影响减贫的全球性研究。本文得出三个主要结论。（1）环境对减贫至关重要。面板回归表明，植被活力提高10%，与农村地区贫困人口比例下降近0.7个百分点相关，与撒哈拉以南非洲地区下降1个百分点相关。土壤质量提高10%，则与农村地区和撒哈拉以南非洲地区的贫困率下降约2个百分点相关。（2）环境质量对贫困的影响强于其对平均收入的影响，这表明穷人从环境质量的改善中获益不成比例。（3）原地环境质量的改善有利于穷人，这与城市化形成对比。尽管城市化与人均GDP之间存在高度显著且规模可观的相关关系，但它与减贫之间并无显著相关。
